title: Evaluation of the Effect of Generative AI in English Writing
venue: Journal of Education, Humanities and Social Sciences
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether generative AI can improve English writing instruction and student writing outcomes in high school classrooms. The central question is how AI-assisted writing evaluation and support affect writing quality, student perceptions, and teachers’ ability to provide personalized feedback and lesson planning.

The intervention involved the Spark Desk AI tool from Iflytek, along with other generative AI tools mentioned in the classroom (Sora, Quillbot, Grammarly, ChatGPT). In the experimental condition, teachers used AI to evaluate writing, generate diagnostic feedback, and support essay instruction; in the control condition, the teacher conducted writing lessons and feedback without AI support. The study also collected semi-structured interview data from students to understand their experiences with AI-assisted writing lessons.

The participants were students from two first-year high school classes in China, with teachers who had prior EFL and English writing experience. The setting was classroom-based English writing instruction focused on the Chinese college entrance exam genre of “continue the story.” Quantitative comparisons of writing performance and error patterns, combined with interview responses, suggested that AI-assisted instruction improved writing outcomes, reduced some error types, and was viewed positively by students, though participants also noted limitations such as mechanical feedback and difficulty using resources. The paper concludes that generative AI can support personalized writing feedback and teacher planning, but it should be used carefully to avoid bias and to preserve human guidance and students’ higher-order thinking development.

identified_tools.name: SparkDesk
identified_tools.description: An AI writing analysis and feedback system by iFlytek that provides diagnostic reports, personalized writing suggestions, and whole-class performance summaries.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in a high school English writing classroom as the generative AI tool for evaluating student essays, generating personalized feedback/resources, and supporting teacher analysis in an experimental comparison with a non-AI control condition.

findings.finding_summary: In the short-run comparison, the AI-assisted class showed a downward trend in writing error frequency and number of errors relative to the traditional class, especially for verb tense and verb form errors. The paper also reports that SparkDesk produced individualized diagnostic reports and teacher-facing whole-class summaries, but it does not provide a formal effect size.
findings.measure: Writing error frequency and number of errors in composition tasks; diagnostic feedback quality
findings.sample_size: 100 samples collected for evaluation; two first-year high school classes

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot used for text generation, feedback, and language support.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed among the generative AI tools used to support students in explaining and improving essay writing during the experimental group lesson; the paper does not isolate ChatGPT-specific implementation details or results.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI chatbot/writing assistance tools used for grammar checking, paraphrasing, content generation, and writing feedback when no single product is being distinguished.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a general label for several AI writing tools discussed in the paper, including AI chatbots and automated writing assistance functions in English writing instruction.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods classroom study with pre/post and interview data, but the paper reports limited methodological detail and no formal statistical effect sizes in the text provided. The evidence is useful for implementation context, but the causal strength is modest.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper claims improved writing performance and reduced errors in the AI-assisted class, but the magnitude is not quantified clearly enough to judge as modest or large. Based on the reported classroom gains and personalized feedback effects, the impact appears potentially meaningful but still uncertain.
